saa-med-301.text: An event analysis architecture requires that a stream's data can be RELIDOS for new consumer applications up to 7 days after ingestion (replay), and that several consumers process the same stream independently. Which service meets these requirements?
options: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with extended retention period
Amazon SQS Standard with DLQ
Amazon Kinesis Firehose Date
Amazon SNS with multiple entries
saa-med-301.explanation: A) Correct: Data Streams retains records (24h by standard, extendable up to 365 (b) Incorrect: no SQS the message consumed is missing from the row — there is no replay or multiple consumers of the same data. C) Incorrect: Firehose delivers and discards — does not retain stream for rereading. D) Incorrect: SNS is immediate push for subscribers; messages are not retained for later rereading.

saa-med-302.text: A company needs to calculate aggregate metrics (e.g. total sales per window of 1 minute) on a stream of the Kinesis EM TEMPO REAL, using SQL or a stream processing framework, and send the results to dashboards. Which service performs this continuous processing with time windows?
options: Amazon Athena consulting the stream directly
AWS Glue Crawler scheduled every minute
Amazon QuickSight reading the stream
Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink Kinesis Data Analytics)
saa-med-302.explanation: (a) Incorrect: Athena refer to EM data REPOUSO no S3, no streams on the move. B) Incorrect: Crawler catalog metadata; neither processes nor aggregates streams. C) Incorrect: QuickSight view data, do not process streams with windows. D) Correct: Managed Flink processes streams in real time with state and time windows (SQL/Java/Python), the case of exact use of window aggregations.

saa-med-303.text: An application consisting of API Gateway, several functions Lambda and calls to DynamoDB is with slow responses intermittently. VISUALIZAR the path of each request between the services and identify exactly which component adds latency. Which service provides this distributed tracking?
options: Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights
AWS X-Ray, with service map and trace analysis
AWS CloudTrail
AWS Configure
saa-med-303.explanation: A) Incorrect: Logs Insights consults logs, but does not correlate the journey of a multiple-service requisition. B) Correct: X-Ray tracks end-to-end requisitions (distributed tracking), mounts the service map and shows the latency of each segment — the exact tool to find the gargalo. C) Incorrect: CloudTrail audit calls from API for governance ('who did what'), no latency of application requests. D) Incorrect: Config tracks resource configuration, no performance.

saa-med-304.text: What is the fundamental difference between Amazon CloudWatch and the AWS X-Ray in monitoring an application?
options: The CloudWatch Metric collection, logs and alarms about resources and applications; X-Ray tracks individual end-to-end requirements between services (distributed tracking))
X-Ray replaces the CloudWatch in serverless architectures
The CloudWatch is paid and X-Ray is always free
The X-Ray collects metrics of CPU and memory of the instances EC2
saa-med-304.explanation: A) Correct: they are complementary — CloudWatch responds 'how are my resources' (metrics/logs/alarms) and X-Ray responds 'where it went and where it took ESTA Incorrect: they complement each other; the X-Ray does not cover metrics or alarms. CloudWatch (with the Agent for Memory).

saa-med-305.text: A team uses the AWS X-Ray and wants to filter and group requisition traces of a specific client (e.g. search for all traces in which customer_id = '123') to investigate complaints of slowness. Which feature of X-Ray allows indexing these values for search?
options: Segment Metadata, which is automatically indexed
Annotations (annotations) added to segments, which are indexed and usable in filter expressions
CloudWatch Dashboards
Sampling rules with rate of 100%
saa-med-305.explanation: A) Incorrect: metadata is stored in the tracks but NOT indexed — not used for search filter. B) Correct: annotations are key-value pairs INDEXADOS by X-Ray, exactly to filter/group traces (e.g. annotation.customer_id = "123"). C) Incorrect: dashboards display metrics; do not filter traces by business attribute. D) Incorrect: sampling defines QUANTAS requests are tracked, not how to fetch them.

saa-med-306.text: An application in AWS Elastic Beanstalk needs to receive new versions SEM downtime and SEM reduce the capacity available during deployment; in case of failure, rollback should be fast and safe. The temporary cost of doubling instances during deployment is acceptable. Which deployment policy best meets these requirements?
options: At eleven
Rolling
Immutable
Rolling with additional batch
saa-med-306.explanation: A) Incorrect: All at once drops and updates all instances together — downtime cause. B) Incorrect: Rolling updates in batches, REDUZINDO the capacity available during the deployment. C) Correct: Immutable creates a new complete set of instances with the new version in parallel; only change when healthy — total capacity maintained and fast rollback (just discard the new ones). D) Incorrect: maintains capacity, but old instances are updated in place — slower and more risky rollback than Immutable.

saa-med-307.text: A team wants to test a new version of the application in Elastic Beanstalk in a separate environment identical to that of production and, after validating, promote the new version by exchanging traffic almost instantly, with the possibility of reversing at the same speed. Elastic Beanstalk implements this blue/green pattern?
options: Configure Rolling deployment with batch 100%
Use the 'Swap environment URLs' feature between the blue and green environments
Enable the Managed Platform Updates
Reimplant previous version by console
saa-med-307.explanation: A) Incorrect: rolling with batch of 100% is equal to all-at-once in the same environment — it is not blue/green. B) Correct: Beanstalk allows you to clone the environment, deploy the new version in the clone (green) and exchange URLs/CNAME Incorrect: Managed Platform Updates updates the PLATAFORMA (SO/runtime), no application versions. D) Incorrect: Reimplanting the previous version is slow rollback, not the blue/green pattern requested.

saa-med-308.text: A web application in Elastic Beanstalk needs to perform long tasks (image processing) without blocking requests HTTP The team wants Beanstalk to also manage the infrastructure of these tasks in the background. Elastic Beanstalk offers for this?
options: Increase the timeout of ALB to wait for processing
Create a Worker Environment, which consumes tasks from a row Amazon SQS managed by Beanstalk
Move processing to edge functions with CloudFront Functions
Use instances Spot in the same web environment
saa-med-308.explanation: A) Incorrect: arresting the request HTTP Waiting for processing is anti-standard — degrades the experience and bursts timeouts.B) Correct: Beanstalk has the Tier 'Worker Environment': the Web Tier sends the task to a queue SQS and the worker processes in background, with daemon managed by Beanstalk himself. C) Incorrect: CloudFront Functions run milliseconds of logic on the edge — unfeasible for image processing. D) Incorrect: Spot changes the purchase model, does not solve the coupling between requisition and processing.

saa-med-309.text: In which scenario the Amazon MQ is preferable to Amazon SQS/SNS?
options: When the application is new (greenfield) and born in the cloud, searching for almost unlimited scale
When an existing application depends on standard messaging protocols (JMS, AMQP, MQTT, STOMP) and the goal is to migrate without rewriting the message layer
When fan-out is needed for millions of subscribers
When the requirement is serverless queue with unlimited throughput
saa-med-309.explanation: A) Incorrect: for new applications in the cloud, the same AWS recommends SQS/SNS (serverless, larger scale, lower operational cost). Amazon MQ exists for compatibility — managed ActiveMQ/RabbitMQ brokers that speak standard protocols, allowing you to migrate legacy applications without changing code. C) Incorrect: massive fan-out is the territory of SNS. D) Incorrect: the MQ is based on brokers with defined capacity, not an unlimited serverless row.

saa-med-310.text: A company will implement the Amazon MQ (ActiveMQ) for a critical application and requires that the broker remain available even with the failure of a Availability Zone. What configuration ensures this?
options: A single instance broker with daily backups
Two independent brokers in different regions with DNS manual
Active/standby broker implemented in multiple AZs, with automatic failover
Increase the size of the single broker instance
saa-med-310.explanation: A) Incorrect: single instance in an AZ is exactly the single point of failure that you want to eliminate. B) Incorrect: independent brokers without state replication and with DNS manual do not give automatic failover or consistency. Amazon MQ offers active deployment/standby multi-AZ: if active broker AZ fails, standby automatically assumes. D) Incorrect: higher instance improves capacity, not availability.

saa-med-311.text: A financial institution requires that cryptographic keys used in AWS stay in validated hardware FIPS 140-2 Level 3, of single-tenant tenant with sole control of the institution — neither AWS which service meets this compliance requirement?
options: AWS KMS with keys managed by AWS
AWS Secrets Manager
AWS CloudHSM
AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)
saa-med-311.explanation: (a) Incorrect: KMS standard uses multi-tenant HSMs (level validation) 2 mostly, with operation managed by AWS) — does not answer 'single-tenant with exclusive control'.: Secrets Manager keep secrets (signs/credential), not a HSM. (c) Correct: or CloudHSM provides dedicated HSMs of single tenant, FIPS 140-2 Level 3, in which only the customer possesses and controls the keys. D) Incorrect: ACM certified management TLS, non-cryptographic hardware modules.

saa-med-312.text: A company wants to continue using the native integration of AWS KMS with the services of the AWS (S3, EBS, RDS), but it needs that the key material resides in dedicated HSMs under its control, by regulatory requirement. What resource combines the two worlds?
options: KMS multi-region keys
AWS KMS Custom Key Store, supported in a cluster AWS CloudHSM
Asymmetrical keys of the KMS
AWS Sign
saa-med-312.explanation: A) Incorrect: multi-Region keys replicate keys between regions — do not change where the key material resides. B) Correct: Custom Key Store connects the KMS to a cluster CloudHSM customer: services continue to use the API of the KMS, but the keys live in the dedicated HSMs. C) Incorrect: asymmetric keys change the type of encryption, not the residence of the material. D) Incorrect: Signer is for code signature, without relation to the requirement.
